newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia raises base price for electric selloff.
newsitem.headline: Colombia raises base price for electric selloff.

text.p: A privatization official said Tuesday that the base price for the government's 56.7 percent stake in Empresas de Energia del Pacifico (Epsa), the leading power company in southwest Colombia, had been raised by 10 percent.

A sale date of May 18 has been set for the government's share in the power company, which has an installed capacity of 900 megawatts and generates and distributes electricity throughout Valle de Cauca province, one of Colombia's leading industrial hubs and an area seen as boasting enormous growth potential.

Juan Fernando Bonilla, head of Colombia's power plant privatization program, said that with the 10 percent increase, Epsa had now been valued by the government at a total of $550 million. He did not elaborate, but that would put the minimum price for the government stake in the company at $311.8 million.
The price hike was based, at least in part, on Epsa's better- than-expected financial results last year, Bonilla told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said there had been no negative reaction to the new price from potential bidders thus far.
